metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes or bullish sentiment; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- When sentiment is negative (especially >50% negative in recent 18 days), model tends to overreact with high early forecasts; apply downward bias of 3–5% to first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use moving average of prior 5 days as floor.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is negative.
- Mean reversion is strong in 7–14 day horizon; if forecast is >1.5σ above 30-day moving average, reduce by 10–20% for next 7 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1) triggers model overconfidence; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days if sentiment flips within 5 days.
- If true outcome shows “outlier” (e.g., <30% of historical range), model often ignores it; apply outlier suppression: if true value < 1.5x median of last 18 days, reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5 days.
